chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Hammad ibn Isa from Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah and Bukayr, the two sons of Ayn, that they heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying:

Regarding alms-tax: as for gold, there is no alms-tax in less than twenty dinars; when it reaches twenty dinars, half a dinar is due. There is no alms-tax in less than two hundred dirhams; when it reaches two hundred dirhams, five dirhams are due. Whatever increases beyond that is calculated accordingly. In two hundred dirhams and forty dirhams (excluding one dirham), there are not five dirhams; when it reaches two hundred and forty dirhams, six dirhams are due. When it reaches two hundred and eighty dirhams, seven dirhams are due, and whatever increases beyond that is calculated on this basis. And so is gold, and all gold. Alms-tax is only on deposited gold and silver when a full year has passed over it; then it is due. And if a year has not passed over it, there is nothing due in it.
ai.seo_question: What are the minimum thresholds and calculation rules for zakat on gold and silver in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the precise nisab and zakat rates for gold (20 dinars) and silver (200 dirhams), establishing a proportional calculation method for amounts exceeding these thresholds. It emphasizes the condition of *hawl* (lunar year), clarifying that zakat is levied on stored wealth only after a full year has passed, a principle central to Shia jurisprudence regarding movable assets. The text underscores the distinction between mere possession and the accumulation of wealth subject to purification, reflecting the practical application of Quranic obligations in early Islamic economic life.
